reviewBoundary: Eight explicitly authored complete original practices: four paired readings with five four-option questions per passage and four ten-gap/fifteen-word passages. Same-author evidence, lexical, grammar and distractor audit; frozen originals supply level and task rules only. No independent teacher/learner calibration, official CET provenance, publication or production approval is claimed.

units.title: 四级阅读：院中鸽子的路线与信封邮戳

materials.title: The Gap in the Courtyard
materials.text:
For several weeks, a college caretaker watched pigeons reach a feeding area by walking around a low fence. When one panel was removed for repairs, a gap offered a shorter route. Some birds continued around the remaining fence at first, even though the opening was wide enough for them.

A student observing the change suggested that the birds had failed to see the gap. The caretaker was less certain. A bird could notice an opening without immediately choosing it. The familiar route had already led safely to food. On later mornings, more birds used the gap, sometimes following another bird through it.

The student began recording routes rather than writing only that the pigeons had learned. She noted whether each bird arrived alone or with others and whether people were standing near the opening. She could not confidently recognise every individual bird, so she did not describe a change in the group total as proof that each bird had changed its own behaviour.

The caretaker also changed where he stood during observation. Remaining near the opening could itself make some birds hesitate, so the student described the observer’s location in her notes. She did not treat a closer view as automatically a better one. A clear account needed to include the possibility that watching from a convenient position had changed the situation being watched, even though nobody had intended to direct the birds.

When the panel was replaced, the shorter route closed. The student recorded that change too. Her account now connected choices with the available path, companions and disturbance. It did not claim that pigeons always preferred habit or always copied one another. The useful discovery was how many different explanations had initially been hidden inside the simple observation that some birds took the long way.

questions.prompt: Why was continuing around the fence not necessarily evidence of failing to see the gap?
options: The caretaker had moved all food outside the courtyard.
The gap was too narrow for any bird.
A familiar route could remain an acceptable choice after an opening was noticed.
questions.explanation: C正确：发现新口不必立即选，旧路已有安全得食经验。B口足够宽；A食物区仍同；D只移一板。

questions.prompt: Which information did the student add to the route record?
options: Whether birds arrived with companions and people stood near the gap.
The exact age of every pigeon.
The caretaker’s favourite kind of food.
The height of every college building.
questions.explanation: A正确：第三段记录同行和缺口附近人的情况。B不能认每只，没龄数；C无偏好记录；D不相关且未记。

questions.prompt: Why could group totals not prove individual learning?
options: The food had not been observed at all.
The student could not reliably identify every individual.
questions.explanation: D正确：无法逐只确认，就不能将总体变比当每只改变。A已有得食路线；B有同行；C后装回板。

questions.prompt: What does “disturbance” refer to in the final paragraph?
options: The permanent shape of the food container.
Factors such as nearby people that might affect the birds’ choices.
The colour of the replacement panel.
A complete loss of the student’s notes.
questions.explanation: B正确：前段人在缺口旁等可能干扰路线选择，末段统称disturbance。A未谈容器形；D无丢笔记；C没颜色证据。

questions.prompt: What is the main point of the passage?
options: A group change always demonstrates learning by every member.
A visible behaviour can have several plausible explanations that observation should distinguish.
The shortest available route must be the route every animal prefers.
questions.explanation: C正确：全文从单因解释扩到路径、同伴、扰动及识别局限。B后来更多通过；A明确不能；D一开始就有绕路反例。

materials.title: The Date on the Envelope
materials.text:
When archivist Ella sorted a box of family letters, she found one envelope with a clear postmark but no date on the letter inside. A volunteer proposed using the postmark as the date the letter had been written. Ella added a note instead: the mark showed when the postal service processed the envelope, not necessarily when the writer had put the words on paper.

The contents offered another clue. The writer described a concert as “last night”, and a newspaper gave a date for that event. Yet the family had sometimes reused envelopes for storing unrelated papers. Ella therefore checked whether the greeting, address and subject made this letter likely to belong to this envelope.

A crease matched the fold of the enclosed sheet, and the recipient’s name agreed. These details supported the connection but did not make the writing date certain. The letter could have waited before posting, and the concert account might not have been sent immediately.

Ella photographed the envelope and sheet together before storing them in separate protective sleeves. Each received a linked identifier, so protection would not break the documented association. The image recorded how they had arrived, but the catalogue still described the possibility of earlier reuse. Keeping two things together in a collection could preserve evidence of their relationship; it could not by itself prove that the relationship had begun when the letter was originally sent.

The catalogue recorded the postmark date in a field for postal evidence and gave a proposed writing period with an explanation. A reader could inspect the basis of the estimate instead of receiving one apparently exact date. Ella had not made the record less useful by keeping the categories separate. She had made it possible to tell which information came directly from the object and which had been inferred by the archive.

questions.prompt: What did the postmark directly establish?
options: The exact hour the writer began the letter.
That the envelope had never been reused.
The date of the concert described inside.
When the postal service processed the envelope.
questions.explanation: D正确：首段明确邮戳证处理信封时点。A不证写作时刻；C音乐会另有报纸；B家庭会复用信封。

questions.prompt: Why did Ella check whether the letter belonged to the envelope?
options: The family sometimes used old envelopes to store other papers.
The volunteer had already destroyed the sheet.
Every family letter had the same greeting.
questions.explanation: A正确：复用信封使内容匹配需另核。C邮戳清楚；B未毁；D无全同称呼。

questions.prompt: What role did the matching crease and recipient’s name play?
options: They proved there had been no delay before posting.
They supported the link between objects without settling the date.
They fixed the writing date to the exact minute.
They made the newspaper date irrelevant.
questions.explanation: B正确：褶与名字支持归属但不定写作时日，可能久放才邮。A未排等待；D新闻仍线索；C无分钟精度。

questions.prompt: How was the catalogue entry organised?
options: It listed the volunteer as the letter’s author.
It silently replaced the postmark with the concert date.
It omitted every date because none could be exact.
It separated the direct postal date from an explained estimate of writing time.
questions.explanation: D正确：邮证字段存邮戳，写作给估计范围和理由。B无暗换；C并未全不记；A作者身份未改。

questions.prompt: What does Ella’s approach enable?
options: A guarantee that all family envelopes held their original contents.
Readers to assume that every processed letter was written that day.
Readers to distinguish object evidence from archival inference.
A claim that newspaper dates are always unreliable.
questions.explanation: C正确：末句直接区分实物所得与档案推论。A复用可能仍在；B正反此假设；D新闻证据未被泛否。

units.title: 四级阅读：攀岩路线标记与旅馆布草统计

materials.title: Which Holds Belong to the Route?
materials.text:
At a college climbing wall, coloured holds marked different routes. A beginner, Mara, chose a blue route but stopped when two blue holds appeared far apart. She thought the route must require a jump beyond her reach. An instructor asked her to read the route card, which named the start, finish and a permitted use of the wall’s broad surface between holds.

Mara had assumed that every movement required touching another blue plastic shape. The card described a different task. With guidance during the supervised lesson, she tried the permitted intermediate position and found a way to continue. The distant hold had not moved closer; her interpretation of the available route had changed.

The instructor then showed two neighbouring blue routes. Their colours alone did not distinguish them, so each had a numbered starting card and a separate finish label. The club added these labels after members had reported confusion in photographs, where similarly coloured holds seemed to form one continuous path.

The club kept old route cards after changing a route, with their dates marked. A photograph from an earlier session could otherwise appear to contradict a current instruction. Members could ask which version a picture showed. The record was not a substitute for checking the wall on the day, but it helped explain why a familiar colour and hold arrangement in an old image might no longer describe the challenge presently offered.

For the next session, Mara chose by the route card and asked about unfamiliar instructions before beginning. She no longer treated a colour as a complete explanation. The wall still offered a physical challenge, and the lesson did not promise that every route would suit her. It helped her identify which challenge had actually been set, rather than spend effort solving a harder task created by a missing assumption.

questions.prompt: What initially made Mara think a large jump was necessary?
options: The instructor had removed every route card.
She assumed each movement had to reach another blue plastic hold.
The blue holds had changed position during her climb.
She had selected the instructor’s most advanced route deliberately.
questions.explanation: B正确：第二段交代她把只碰蓝塑料点当规则，遗漏允许中间墙面用法。A有卡；C点没移；D无刻意选最难。

questions.prompt: What changed when she found a way forward?
options: Her understanding of the permitted task.
questions.explanation: D正确：远点没变，路线可用动作解释改变。A、B、C皆非叙述变化。

questions.prompt: Why did the club use numbered starts and separate finishes?
options: Colours were no longer visible on the wall.
The same colour could be used for neighbouring routes.
Every route ended on the same hold.
questions.explanation: C正确：两相邻蓝线不能只靠色分，号与终点标签辅助。B没禁拍；A颜色在；D分别标终点。

questions.prompt: What does “missing assumption” mean here?
options: An unstated or overlooked belief about what the task allowed.
A missing safety mat described in the card.
An unavailable photograph of the instructor.
questions.explanation: A正确：她自行假定每步仅可蓝点，使任务变难，需读卡问规则。B不是坏点；C未说垫缺失；D非导师照片。

questions.prompt: What lesson does Mara take to the next session?
options: Every route will become easy if its colour is blue.
A photograph always describes a route more completely than its card.
Route labels remove the need for supervised instruction.
Understanding the instructions helps identify the actual challenge before attempting it.
questions.explanation: D正确：先按卡选、问不懂，识别真正任务；体能挑战仍在。A无全易保证；B照片曾混淆；C本例有监督指导未替代。

materials.title: Counting Linen at the Inn
materials.text:
A small inn’s manager believed that its laundry service had lost towels. The store count was lower than the previous week, although the laundry’s delivery record listed the expected total. Before making a claim, receptionist Tomas checked where the count had been taken.

The previous count included clean towels on room-service carts. The new count covered only the shelves. Some clean towels were also already in rooms prepared for arriving guests. Comparing these totals as if they described the same stock location created an apparent shortage.

Tomas proposed separate categories: clean in store, clean assigned to rooms, in use, and awaiting laundry. A towel moved from one category to another without becoming a newly purchased or missing object. Staff recorded transfers during a short trial instead of repeatedly adding new deliveries to a shelf number that excluded every transfer out.

The revised record did identify two damaged towels removed from service, which had not been noted earlier. It did not find evidence that the laundry had lost the difference originally alleged. The manager informed the service of the corrected count and introduced a reason field for removals.

The trial also used a named time for each count. A delivery arriving halfway through a check could make one shelf seem fuller than another without any real inconsistency. Staff noted incoming and outgoing movements during the count rather than pretending the store stood still while they worked. The added record did not make every error impossible. It gave a later reviewer a way to ask whether a difference came from timing, location or an actual unexplained absence.

The episode changed how the inn used a simple total. A lower number could represent a loss, a legitimate movement or a change in the boundary of the count. Checking which question a figure answered was part of responsible administration, not a delay before the “real” work began.

questions.prompt: Why did the two initial towel totals create a misleading comparison?
options: The laundry had delivered no towels that week.
The counts covered different locations and categories.
Staff counted the same towels twice on both occasions.
questions.explanation: C正确：前含车上，后仅架上，另有已配客房，统计边界异。A送货记录有预期数；B无颜色变化；D非两次都重复计。

questions.prompt: What did the new categories make clear?
options: Every towel assigned to a room had been discarded.
Movement between locations need not mean a purchase or a loss.
Only shelf stock could be counted in any circumstance.
Laundry delivery records should never be used.
questions.explanation: B正确：分类转移仍是同物非新买或丢失。A房用非弃；C可按目的分各类；D配送记录仍证据之一。

questions.prompt: What genuine removal was found?
options: Two damaged towels taken out of service without an earlier note.
A delivery sent to another inn.
All room-service carts sold to guests.
A week of laundry that had not been returned.
questions.explanation: A正确：第四段两坏巾退出未记，后增原因栏。B无错送；C无售车；D未发现原指控洗衣丢差额证据。

questions.prompt: How did the manager respond to the revised evidence?
options: She repeated the original accusation without checking.
She removed the new categories immediately.
She corrected the claim to the laundry and documented reasons for removals.
She announced that missing towels could never occur.
questions.explanation: C正确：通知洗衣方更正并增退出原因记录。A与事实相反；B采纳类别；D没排除今后一切丢失。

questions.prompt: What broader point does the passage make?
options: A lower total always proves theft.
The meaning of a total depends on what and where it counts.
More categories guarantee that no object can be lost.
Administrative counts have no practical value.
questions.explanation: B正确：末段低数可丢、移动或范围变，必须问数字回答何问。A无盗窃证且绝对化；D分类查出真坏巾有用；C分类不保证永不丢。

units.title: 六级阅读：模型解释的因果边界与图书馆罚款评估

materials.title: A Reason for a Prediction
materials.text:
An explanation of a prediction can answer more than one question. It may show which inputs a model relied on, offer an understandable summary of its calculation, or claim that changing something in the world would change the outcome. These are related projects, but success at one does not automatically establish success at the others.

Consider a fictional system predicting whether a delivery will arrive late. Its explanation highlights the recipient’s postcode. Changing that input while holding the others fixed may alter the model’s output. This demonstrates a form of dependence within the model. It does not prove that changing the postcode printed on an otherwise unchanged parcel would improve a real delivery. The postcode may stand in for road conditions, depot arrangements or other factors the explanation has not separated.

A further difficulty is that some edited input combinations may not resemble any plausible delivery. A convenient test of the software can therefore be a poor description of an intervention available to a dispatcher. The explanation should state which question it answers and what assumptions connect it with possible action.

The researchers also compared different kinds of explanation for the same prediction. A short statement might be easier to understand while omitting interactions that a developer needed to examine. A detailed account could expose those interactions but overwhelm a person trying to decide whether to question a delivery estimate. Neither audience’s need made the other account automatically false. The report named its audience and the use for which an explanation had been prepared.

For possible action, the team asked what a dispatcher could actually change. Reassigning a depot or altering a route was different from changing a label in a test input. A real intervention might also alter several model inputs together. An explanation based on holding everything else fixed therefore required a further argument before it could recommend that intervention. The most useful result was sometimes a warning that the current information did not yet identify an effective operational change.

This does not make an input-level account useless. It can help developers identify an unexpected reliance and help users question the system. Its value increases when it supports a specific form of scrutiny instead of claiming to reveal every cause of the event predicted. A clear explanation may expose the next uncertainty rather than close the investigation.

questions.prompt: What distinction frames the passage?
options: Delivery outcomes cannot be studied using models.
Every understandable explanation is necessarily a causal proof.
An explanation can answer only one kind of question in principle.
A model’s input dependence is not automatically a causal account of events in the world.
questions.explanation: D正确：开头区分依赖、可理解摘要、真实干预因果，彼此不自动证明。B将易懂等于因果；C有多项目；A未否定建模。

questions.prompt: What does changing the postcode input establish in the example?
options: That every delivery with the new label would be faster.
A dependence of the model’s output on that input under the test.
That a dispatcher can move every depot immediately.
questions.explanation: B正确：软件输出随输入改是模型内依赖；不证现实换标签改善。A过度因果；C邮区可能代理道路；D无仓站可即移保证。

questions.prompt: Why might some input edits fail to guide practical intervention?
options: The combinations may not correspond to plausible real deliveries.
All dispatchers use the same postcode.
The software cannot accept edited information.
The original explanation contained no highlighted input.
questions.explanation: A正确：某些编辑组合现实不合理，软件测试不等同可行动作。C测试可改；B无统一邮区；D明确高亮邮区。

questions.prompt: What does “stand in for” mean in paragraph 2?
options: Prevent every variable from being measured.
Act as a proxy for other related factors.
Arrive before the intended delivery date.
questions.explanation: C正确：邮区可代表道路或仓站相关因素。A非替换包裹；B非阻所有测量；D不是提前到货语义。

questions.prompt: How can an input-level explanation still be useful?
options: It can reveal unexpected reliance and support targeted questioning of the model.
It guarantees that the highlighted input is the only real cause.
It makes every implausible test combination actionable.
It eliminates the need to state assumptions.
questions.explanation: A正确：末段助开发发现意外依赖，用户质疑，限具体审查。B非唯一真实因；C未使不合理组合可行；D仍需声明假设。

materials.title: What Changed When the Fine Disappeared?
materials.text:
A fictional library removed overdue fines for ordinary books while retaining reminders and a procedure for long-unreturned items. Six months later, it recorded more active borrowers. Supporters wanted to describe the increase as the effect of ending fines. The evaluation team welcomed the figure but asked what else had changed.

During the same period, the library had extended its evening hours and reopened a renovated children’s room. These changes could also affect attendance. A neighbouring library offered a possible comparison, but it served a different population and had not followed the same opening schedule. A comparison group could inform the analysis without being a perfect duplicate of the original site.

The team also distinguished registered membership from active borrowing. Some people had held cards for years without using them. Counting newly issued cards alone would miss a return by such users. Staff defined the outcome before deciding which total best represented it.

Interviewees described reduced anxiety about borrowing, but those accounts came from people willing to speak to the team. They revealed experiences worth considering without measuring the response of every resident. The report combined these accounts with records and made the limits of each visible.

An evaluation also needed to specify what success meant. More active borrowers was one possible access outcome; the availability of requested books was another. A policy might improve one measure while leaving a different question unresolved. The report listed these outcomes separately instead of converting them into a single impression that the library had become better in every respect.

For future observation, the team proposed retaining consistent definitions and recording changes to hours, services and membership alongside the borrowing totals. This would not recreate a world in which the policy had never changed. It would make later comparisons more informative and reduce avoidable confusion about what had been counted. Staff could also ask why some people still did not borrow. An improvement for visible users did not establish that all barriers had disappeared for residents absent from the records. The unanswered question was a reason for further enquiry, not a reason to suppress the improvements already documented.

Ending fines remained a decision the library could defend on stated access grounds. The evaluation did not need to pretend that the six-month increase isolated a single cause. It could document what changed, investigate plausible effects and leave the size of the policy’s separate contribution open.

questions.prompt: Why was the borrowing increase insufficient to isolate the effect of ending fines?
options: The library had stopped recording borrowing entirely.
Hours and facilities had also changed during the period.
The library served no existing cardholders.
questions.explanation: B正确：同时延晚间开放、重开儿童室，可能共同影响。A有记录；C提醒保留；D有多年持卡者。

questions.prompt: How was the neighbouring library treated?
options: As proof that the two populations were identical.
As a replacement for all local records.
As the authority deciding the first library’s policy.
As a comparison with differences that still needed consideration.
questions.explanation: D正确：邻馆可提供信息但人群时段异，非完美复制。A明确不同；C不负责决策；B未取代本地证据。

questions.prompt: Why distinguish active borrowers from new cardholders?
options: Every issued card was used immediately.
Old cardholders were prohibited from returning.
Existing members returning to use could be missed by counting only new cards.
The outcome was the number of renovated rooms.
questions.explanation: C正确：旧卡久不用后返回不算新发卡，需按活跃借阅定义。A无即用保证；B可返回；D房间是同期变化非借阅结果。

questions.prompt: What limit applies to the interviews?
options: They came from willing participants rather than measuring every resident’s response.
They proved that anxiety had never affected borrowing.
They contained no experiences relevant to access.
They guaranteed the policy had no effect on anyone.
questions.explanation: A正确：愿意受访者样本揭经验但不量全体。B实际有人焦虑减；C经验有考虑价值；D无法据此证明全无效。

questions.prompt: Which report would match the passage’s recommendation?
options: One assigning the whole rise to fines without discussing other changes.
One treating a comparison library as an identical control by definition.
One rejecting all borrowing records because interviews were selective.
One defending access aims while clearly limiting the causal claim supported by the data.
questions.explanation: D正确：目标可辩护、同时不假装单因效应已分离。A过度归因；C记录仍用；B邻馆差异须说明。

units.title: 六级阅读：陶片拼合与音乐推荐中的可见选择

materials.title: The Space Between the Shards
materials.text:
A museum’s fictional reconstruction of a pottery vessel began with fragments whose painted lines seemed to continue across their broken edges. Some pieces also joined physically. The conservator distinguished these two forms of fit: a plausible continuation of decoration did not guarantee that two fragments had once touched.

The proposed vessel profile contained missing sections. Filling those gaps could help visitors understand the overall shape, but the fill was made visibly different from the surviving material. The reconstruction did not manufacture evidence simply by completing an attractive outline. Where more than one profile remained possible, the display described the selected proposal and its alternatives.

A catalogue photograph created a further choice. A view from one side made the vessel look nearly complete, while another exposed a large gap. Neither view was necessarily false, but presenting only the first without explanation would encourage a stronger impression of completeness than the object supported. The publication included multiple views and a diagram identifying restored sections.

The conservator kept a drawing of the fragments before assembly and recorded which edges had been examined. Temporary supports allowed some decisions to be reconsidered without hiding where surviving material ended. This record mattered even if the assembled object looked convincing. A later researcher might have a different reason for grouping fragments or new information about the excavation.

The display also distinguished the vessel’s proposed shape from its proposed use. A narrow opening could support one suggestion without proving exactly what people had stored inside. Evidence from residues or a securely documented context would answer different questions. The reconstruction could organise those questions, but it did not make additional evidence unnecessary. Visitors were invited to compare the supported relationships rather than admire completeness as the only sign of a successful conservation project. Some missing sections remained open because filling them would add confidence to appearance without adding comparable support to the historical account.

The arrangement was useful for discussing how the vessel might have been made and used. It was less useful as an unquestionable template for classifying every loose fragment found nearby. Similar decoration could occur on another vessel, and a fragment’s excavation context still mattered. Reconstruction was a reasoned proposal assembled from evidence; once built and photographed, it did not become an independent source confirming all the assumptions used to create it.

questions.prompt: What distinction did the conservator make?
options: A continuation of painted design and an actual physical join.
An object’s height and the length of its museum label.
The ownership of the museum and the ownership of the camera.
The age of a visitor and the age of a fragment.
questions.explanation: A正确：首段图案似续与边缘物理拼合是不同证据。B、C、D不是文中区分。

questions.prompt: Why was the added fill visibly different?
options: It had been found in a separate excavation.
It was intended to hide every original painted line.
It helped viewers distinguish restoration from surviving material.
It proved that only one vessel shape was possible.
questions.explanation: C正确：缺段补形有助理解，但须与存料区分免造证据。A补料非另挖得；B不为遮原绘；D可仍有多形。

questions.prompt: What concern arose from a single favourable photograph?
options: It could never show a real object.
It could imply more completeness than the full object warranted.
It would make all alternative profiles physically impossible.
It would necessarily change the fragments’ material.
questions.explanation: B正确：单侧近完整照可强化超证据完整感，故多视图修复图。A该视图本身可真；D照片不变材料；C不排别形。

questions.prompt: Why should nearby loose fragments not automatically be classified from the reconstructed form?
options: All pottery in the area came from one vessel by definition.
No fragment can ever be identified after excavation.
The conservator had discarded all physical joins.
Similar decoration and different contexts could leave more than one origin possible.
questions.explanation: D正确：近旁同画也可属别器，还需出土语境，不自动套模板。B非永不可识；C仍有真拼合；A无唯一起源假定。

questions.prompt: What circular reasoning does the ending warn against?
options: Using a diagram to identify restored material.
Treating a built reconstruction as independent confirmation of the assumptions that produced it.
Recording physical joins before selecting a shape.
Showing more than one view of an incomplete object.
questions.explanation: B正确：根据假设拼出的物体不因建成拍照就变独立证明这些假设。A、C、D都是可支持辨证的方法，不是循环。

materials.title: The Song the Listener Never Saw
materials.text:
A music service’s fictional recommendation study examined what users played after receiving a list of suggested tracks. The most frequently chosen song appeared to be the strongest expression of preference. Yet listeners could select only from what the system had placed before them, and items near the top received more attention.

A researcher proposed separating exposure from choice. The log should record which tracks were offered, where they appeared and which were played. Without the first two pieces of information, silence about an unoffered song could be mistaken for rejection. A song absent from the list had not necessarily lost a fair comparison.

The system also learned from past selections. If an early list favoured one style, the resulting plays could lead to more of that style being recommended. This loop might fit a listener well, but it could also narrow the evidence the system later used to describe them. Repeated exposure and genuine preference were not automatically separable from counts alone.

The study tested some varied lists under stated conditions and asked participants about unfamiliar tracks. It did not assume that novelty was always welcome or that a click revealed lasting affection. Listening time, skipping and later choices each offered partial evidence.

The report distinguished discovery from repetition as possible goals. A user building a familiar background playlist might welcome a narrow selection, while someone searching for new artists might prefer a wider range. Those purposes could change between sessions. The system should not interpret the same click as a timeless instruction that every future list must resemble the present one.

An experiment with position required care too. Moving a track higher could alter attention, but the list around it and the listener’s current activity could matter. The study described the conditions of its comparison rather than announce one universal correction for position. A fuller log made these relationships easier to investigate; it did not reveal a person’s private experience without remainder. The recommendation was to retain the history of what had been offered alongside what had been chosen, so that the service’s own interventions remained visible in the evidence from which it continued to learn.

The service could still personalise recommendations. The report’s contribution was to make the process that produced visible choices part of the interpretation. A ranking described as “what the listener wants” needed an account of what the listener had actually had an opportunity to encounter.

questions.prompt: Why was the most-played track not a complete measure of unconstrained preference?
options: Users could play only music they had composed themselves.
Every recommendation appeared in a random position.
The offered selection and its order shaped opportunities to choose.
No listening information had been logged.
questions.explanation: C正确：可选集合由系统给，靠前更被关注，播放不是无条件全域偏好。A无只播自作；B未随机；D有选播日志。

questions.prompt: What should the proposed log distinguish?
options: Which songs were offered, their positions and the choices made.
The price of every recording studio.
The number of instruments in every track.
The time each musician began training.
questions.explanation: A正确：第二段三项就是曝光、位置与播放。B、C、D均非拟加字段。

questions.prompt: What mistake could be made about an unoffered song?
options: Assuming it had been played on another service.
Treating its absence from play records as a rejection by the listener.
questions.explanation: D正确：没机会遇到不等于在公平比较中拒绝。A、B、C均无由不曝光推出的证据。

questions.prompt: How can the recommendation loop narrow later evidence?
options: Every new recommendation makes past records independent of the system.
Early exposure favours a style, its plays lead to more similar recommendations and future observations stay within that narrowed set.
The service must remove all popular styles after one play.
A click automatically establishes permanent affection.
questions.explanation: B正确：第三段曝光选择反馈可使后续样本同型，不一定说明稳定完整偏好。A不是自动独立；C无强制删流行；D点击非持久喜爱。

questions.prompt: What does the study recommend in interpreting visible choices?
options: Assume novelty is always the best goal.
Account for the opportunities the system created and use several bounded indicators.
Treat every skipped track as proof of dislike in all contexts.
questions.explanation: C正确：看系统给过何机会，播放时长跳过后选等都只部分证据。A新颖非总欢迎；B仍可个性化；D跳过不证所有情境厌恶。

units.title: 四级选词：活字排版中的字面与行距
units.instruction: Read the complete passage. Choose an unchanged word from the shared fifteen-word bank for each gap. Each word may be used at most once; five are not needed.

materials.title: Before the Page Was Printed
materials.text:
At a printing-history workshop, replica letters had ____1____ faces standing above their bases. The printing areas were also ____2____ from left to right, so that contact with paper would produce letters facing the normal reading direction.

A line was ____3____ by arranging the separate pieces in the required order. Words were ____4____ apart with blank pieces between them. The instructor distinguished horizontal gaps between words from ____5____, material used to separate lines vertically. The two kinds of spacing solved different layout problems.

Once the page arrangement was complete, it was ____6____ in a frame so that the pieces would not move during printing. The faces were ____7____ before a sheet was pressed against them. The resulting ____8____ was examined for missing letters and unwanted marks.

After the demonstration, the individual pieces were ____9____ back into their storage cases, returned to their assigned places for future use. Leaving them as an unidentified heap would make the next task slower.

The instructor also discussed ____10____, the design of the letter shapes. A different style could change the appearance of the page without changing its wording. The workshop separated visual design, spacing and the mechanics of transferring ink. A printed page was the result of all these choices, not just the number of letters that had been collected.

questions.prompt: Before the Page Was Printed: choose the unchanged word for gap 1.
questions.explanation: faces standing above bases定义raised凸起。fragile易碎、variable可变、mirrored镜像均不表示高于底座；其余词词性或义不符。

questions.prompt: Before the Page Was Printed: choose the unchanged word for gap 2.
questions.explanation: left right reversed for normal reading印迹需mirrored镜像。raised高度不说明左右，spaced为隔开、inked为上墨、locked为锁紧均非方向反转。

questions.prompt: Before the Page Was Printed: choose the unchanged word for gap 3.
questions.explanation: arranging separate pieces required order定义composed排组。distributed是回分各格，与当前组线相反，spaced仅增间隔非完成字序，其他项不表排字。

questions.prompt: Before the Page Was Printed: choose the unchanged word for gap 4.
questions.explanation: apart with blank pieces说明spaced留间距。composed泛排字不特指词间空隙，distributed回放、locked固定均非用空件隔词的动作。

questions.prompt: Before the Page Was Printed: choose the unchanged word for gap 5.
questions.explanation: material separate lines vertically直接定义leading行间铅条。margin为页边非行间，grain纸或木纹、typeface字形设计均不指纵向行距材料。

questions.prompt: Before the Page Was Printed: choose the unchanged word for gap 6.
questions.explanation: so pieces would not move要求locked固定锁紧。inked上墨不防位置移动，mirrored反向、distributed分回均非锁版，其他词不合。

questions.prompt: Before the Page Was Printed: choose the unchanged word for gap 7.
questions.explanation: before sheet pressed faces需inked上墨。locked固定不提供墨，raised凸面是原结构，distributed收字不是印前处理；其他项不表着墨。

questions.prompt: Before the Page Was Printed: choose the unchanged word for gap 8.
questions.explanation: result pressed sheet printed mark为impression印迹。typeface设计、leading材料、margin页边、grain纹理均非这次压印得到的完整结果。

questions.prompt: Before the Page Was Printed: choose the unchanged word for gap 9.
questions.explanation: back storage assigned places returned说明distributed分回。composed是组成版、spaced隔开、locked锁紧、inked上墨，均不表示结束后各归字格。

questions.prompt: Before the Page Was Printed: choose the unchanged word for gap 10.
questions.explanation: design letter shapes直接定义typeface字体设计。grain材料纹、margin页边、leading行距、impression印迹均不是字形风格本身。

units.title: 四级选词：显微镜中的放大与分辨
units.instruction: Read the complete passage. Choose an unchanged word from the shared fifteen-word bank for each gap. Each word may be used at most once; five are not needed.

materials.title: Bigger Is Not Always Clearer
materials.text:
In a microscope lesson, the specimen rested on a glass ____1____, the flat support placed on the instrument’s stage. It had been ____2____ for observation rather than taken straight from a dirty storage container. A thin glass ____3____ lay over it to keep the sample in the intended arrangement.

The viewing area was ____4____ by the instrument’s light. The tutor then identified the ____5____, the lens nearest the specimen. Changing that lens could alter the ____6____, how much larger the image appeared than the object.

A large blurry image still required ____7____, adjustment to bring the relevant plane into a clear view. Even after that adjustment, two very close details might remain indistinguishable. The ability to separate them concerned ____8____, not image size alone.

The tutor also changed ____9____, the difference that made the specimen stand out from its background. Increasing visibility in one way did not automatically improve every property of the picture.

Finally, the class discussed ____10____ from unwanted material on a slide or tool. A mark in the view did not automatically belong to the specimen. The lesson connected what learners saw with preparation, optics and the condition of the sample. Naming the source of an apparent detail was part of observation, not a separate task that could be ignored once the image became large.

questions.prompt: Bigger Is Not Always Clearer: choose the unchanged word for gap 1.
questions.explanation: flat glass support on stage定义slide载玻片。cover是上方薄盖而非下托，objective镜头、focus对焦、contrast对比度均不是承托平板。

questions.prompt: Bigger Is Not Always Clearer: choose the unchanged word for gap 2.
questions.explanation: for observation rather dirty storage说明prepared制备过。illuminated是受光不表示样品先处理，inverted倒置、transmitted传递均非此准备工序。

questions.prompt: Bigger Is Not Always Clearer: choose the unchanged word for gap 3.
questions.explanation: thin glass over sample定义cover盖片。slide是下托，第1空明确占用；objective是物镜不盖住样品，其他词不命名这一上层玻璃。

questions.prompt: Bigger Is Not Always Clearer: choose the unchanged word for gap 4.
questions.explanation: by instrument light直接指illuminated照明。prepared制备不等于照亮，transmitted为透射传递不以viewing area为这句被照受体，其他项无此义。

questions.prompt: Bigger Is Not Always Clearer: choose the unchanged word for gap 5.
questions.explanation: lens nearest specimen定义objective物镜。focus调焦、magnification放大率、resolution分辨率均为光学属性或调整非该镜头名。

questions.prompt: Bigger Is Not Always Clearer: choose the unchanged word for gap 6.
questions.explanation: how much larger image appears定义magnification放大率。resolution可分细节、contrast明暗差、focus焦面都不等于物像大小比例。

questions.prompt: Bigger Is Not Always Clearer: choose the unchanged word for gap 7.
questions.explanation: adjustment relevant plane clear定义focus对焦。contrast区分背景、resolution分离细节不是调整焦面动作，magnification改变尺度也不保证清楚。

questions.prompt: Bigger Is Not Always Clearer: choose the unchanged word for gap 8.
questions.explanation: ability separate close details定义resolution分辨率。magnification只是放大，focus焦面调整、overlap重叠、contrast差异不等同分辨相邻点能力。

questions.prompt: Bigger Is Not Always Clearer: choose the unchanged word for gap 9.
questions.explanation: difference specimen background定义contrast对比度。focus调焦、magnification放大、resolution细节区分都不是背景区别本身；其他词不合释义。

questions.prompt: Bigger Is Not Always Clearer: choose the unchanged word for gap 10.
questions.explanation: unwanted material on slide tool定义contamination污染。overlap重叠可能源于样品排布但不等于外来异物，其他候选不命名材料混入问题。

units.title: 六级选词：价格指数篮子的权重
units.instruction: Read the complete passage. Choose an unchanged word from the shared fifteen-word bank for each gap. Each word may be used at most once; five are not needed.

materials.title: The Basket Behind the Number
materials.text:
A fictional statistics class constructed a price index from a ____1____ of goods and services. The selection was intended to be ____2____ of a stated pattern of purchases, not a claim that every household bought exactly those items.

Prices were compared with a ____3____ period, a named reference point for the index. The inputs also needed to be ____4____ across time. A different package size or changed product could make a simple comparison of the printed price misleading.

The class combined changes into an ____5____ measure rather than publish only unrelated prices. Items were ____6____ according to their shares in the chosen spending pattern. A large increase in a rarely bought item would therefore not automatically count the same as an equal increase in a major expense.

The ____7____ of the basket mattered as well as its weighting. If the selected mix remained unchanged while people altered what they bought, the index continued to answer a question tied to that old mix. Consumers might practise ____8____, replacing a more expensive item with an available alternative, although not every purchase offered that possibility.

A procedure to ____9____ the basket could improve relevance but also change the basis of comparison. The report documented revisions instead of presenting the series as if no design choice had ever changed.

The class described broad price ____10____ within the scope of its index, a rise in the measured price level. It did not equate one index with every household’s experience or with a complete measure of well-being. The number remained useful because its population, items and comparison rules were stated.

questions.prompt: The Basket Behind the Number: choose the unchanged word for gap 1.
questions.explanation: selection goods services for index称basket篮子。expenditure为支出量、composition为组成属性、base为参照期、welfare福利不指那组具体入选商品服务。

questions.prompt: The Basket Behind the Number: choose the unchanged word for gap 2.
questions.explanation: of stated purchases not each household说明representative有代表性。comparable可比不表代表群体，nominal名义、weighted加权均不是对目标购买模式代表关系。

questions.prompt: The Basket Behind the Number: choose the unchanged word for gap 3.
questions.explanation: named reference period定义base基期。composition构成、aggregate总量、volatility波动均不指参照时间，其他词词性或义不合。

questions.prompt: The Basket Behind the Number: choose the unchanged word for gap 4.
questions.explanation: across time且防包装产品改变误比要求comparable可比。representative代表性不保证同质，nominal名义、weighted加权均不说明跨时同口径。

questions.prompt: The Basket Behind the Number: choose the unchanged word for gap 5.
questions.explanation: combined changes rather unrelated prices定义aggregate综合汇总。nominal未作购买力调整不等于多价合成，weighted只指权重设计，其他候选不直接表总体合并。

questions.prompt: The Basket Behind the Number: choose the unchanged word for gap 6.
questions.explanation: according shares major expense不同贡献定义weighted加权。aggregate为汇总属性非每项按占比操作，nominal名义、representative代表性不表示赋相对权数。

questions.prompt: The Basket Behind the Number: choose the unchanged word for gap 7.
questions.explanation: selected mix及basket changes说明composition构成。expenditure支出金额、volatility波动、welfare福利不直接指入篮项目组合；其他名词不合。

questions.prompt: The Basket Behind the Number: choose the unchanged word for gap 8.
questions.explanation: replacing expensive item alternative定义substitution替代。update更新程序、yield产出、expenditure开支均不指改买别物行为。

questions.prompt: The Basket Behind the Number: choose the unchanged word for gap 9.
questions.explanation: basket revision improve relevance定义update更新。yield为产生不是改篮，其他候选无to后这种使选样合时的原形动词。

questions.prompt: The Basket Behind the Number: choose the unchanged word for gap 10.
questions.explanation: rise measured price level直接定义inflation价格通胀。volatility上下波动不一定上涨，welfare整体福利、expenditure所花金额、base基期均非总体物价升。

units.title: 六级选词：问卷措辞与社会期许
units.instruction: Read the complete passage. Choose an unchanged word from the shared fifteen-word bank for each gap. Each word may be used at most once; five are not needed.

materials.title: An Answer in Front of Someone Else
materials.text:
In a fictional survey workshop, a question about personal spending was asked in two settings. In one, an ____1____ sat opposite the participant and read the item aloud. In another, the participant completed a private form without that person watching each answer.

The team did not assume privacy guaranteed a ____2____ answer. People could still misunderstand, forget or prefer not to report. Yet the setting might change pressure to ____3____ to an expected norm rather than describe actual behaviour.

Some responses could appear socially ____4____, presenting the participant in a favourable light. This possibility was especially relevant to a ____5____ topic, one involving information people might be reluctant to discuss. The researchers distinguished that reluctance from a lack of understanding.

They examined the question’s ____6____, how its wording presented the choice and suggested a perspective. A phrase praising one behaviour could make the item less ____7____ than the writers intended. Merely removing an obvious positive adjective would not settle every influence of language.

The time period affected ____8____. Remembering yesterday’s purchases could require a different effort from estimating a whole year. A confident number was not automatically an accurate memory.

The record also separated answers from ____9____, cases where no answer was given. An empty field did not necessarily mean zero spending. Understanding why it was empty could matter to the inference.

Finally, the team asked about ____10____: whether the resulting measure supported the interpretation it was intended to support. An orderly form and a high completion total could be useful without proving this. The exercise treated wording, setting and memory as parts of how survey evidence was produced, not distractions that disappeared once responses had been entered into a table.

questions.prompt: An Answer in Front of Someone Else: choose the unchanged word for gap 1.
questions.explanation: person sits asks aloud定义interviewer访员。context是情境、prompt提示、disclosure披露不是提问的人；其他候选不命名该角色。

questions.prompt: An Answer in Front of Someone Else: choose the unchanged word for gap 2.
questions.explanation: private not guarantee honest frank answer语境需candid坦率。anonymous无名不等于答真，neutral中立不直接指参与者愿直说，desirable受欢迎也非坦诚，其他词不合。

questions.prompt: An Answer in Front of Someone Else: choose the unchanged word for gap 3.
questions.explanation: to expected norm rather actual行为需conform顺从。recall回忆通常不以to norm搭配，prompt为提示需对象，其他候选非to后表遵从规范的原形动作。

questions.prompt: An Answer in Front of Someone Else: choose the unchanged word for gap 4.
questions.explanation: socially及favourable light定义desirable社会赞许的。candid坦率不一定好看，neutral中立、anonymous无名不说明合社会期许；其他词性或义不合。

questions.prompt: An Answer in Front of Someone Else: choose the unchanged word for gap 5.
questions.explanation: reluctant discuss personal information定义sensitive敏感。neutral中性、anonymous匿名、candid坦率均不说明话题令人生顾虑；desirable受赞许不同于披露风险。

questions.prompt: An Answer in Front of Someone Else: choose the unchanged word for gap 6.
questions.explanation: how wording presents choice perspective定义framing框架措辞。context广泛情境、prompt单提示、disclosure披露、recall回想均非这个问题呈现角度过程。

questions.prompt: An Answer in Front of Someone Else: choose the unchanged word for gap 7.
questions.explanation: praising behaviour makes less neutral中立。anonymous无名、candid坦率、desirable合期许都不直接表示题目不偏袒任一行为；其他项不合。

questions.prompt: An Answer in Front of Someone Else: choose the unchanged word for gap 8.
questions.explanation: remember yesterday or year定义recall回忆。nonresponse无答、validity效度、disclosure披露均不是检索过去记忆的过程。

questions.prompt: An Answer in Front of Someone Else: choose the unchanged word for gap 9.
questions.explanation: no answer given直接定义nonresponse未回应。disclosure是披露内容，context情境、recall回想都不指空答状态。

questions.prompt: An Answer in Front of Someone Else: choose the unchanged word for gap 10.
questions.explanation: measure supports intended interpretation定义validity效度。recall记忆、framing措辞、context情境是影响因素非这种解释获得支持的属性，其他词不合。
